MODERATE activity (half_width 14.0-17.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 2-8 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 5-15 range
- taker_buy_share showing imbalance: 0.30-0.40 or 0.60-0.70
- 90-180 minutes from funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC hours (but not 13:30-14:30)
- volume 50-150% of typical
- one or two bars in last 5 moved >4 bps
- Example 1: change_1m +4.3, change_5m +8.5 → actual +2.2 bps. Should quote ±14 bps minimum.
- Example 4: change_1m +13, change_5m -19 → actual +4.9 bps. Should quote ±15 bps minimum.
- Example 6: change_1m -1.3, change_5m +2.4 → actual +7.4 bps. Should quote ±14 bps minimum.

ELEVATED volatility (half_width 18.0-23.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 8
- |change_5m_bps| > 15
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.70 or <0.30
- 30-90 minutes from funding
- during 13:30-14:30 UTC specifically (US cash open)
- volume >150% of typical
- multiple bars in last 5 moved >5 bps
- Example 2: change_1m +7.3, change_5m -13.4, tape 0.64, 60 min to funding → actual +8.5 bps. Need ±19 bps.
- Example 3: change_1m +2.0, change_5m +8.6, tape 0.72, 0 UTC hour → actual -13.1 bps. Need ±21 bps.
- Example 5: change_1m -1.9, change_5m +0.4, tape 0.73 → actual +15.4 bps. Need ±20 bps.

HIGH volatility (half_width 24.0-32.0 bps) for genuine chaos:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15
- |change_5m_bps| > 25
- liquidation cascade visible (extreme selling + volume surge + open interest drop)
- within 30 minutes of funding with large perp basis
- consecutive large moves (3+ bars with |move| > 8 bps)
- taker_buy_share at extremes (>0.85 or <0.15) with high volume
- Example 7: change_1m +2.1, change_5m +1.1, tape 0.85 → actual +31.9 bps. Need ±32 bps minimum.

NEVER quote below 11.0 bps half_width. The data shows that even the calmest minute can move 7-8 bps, and quoting under 11 bps leaves no margin for error.

THE SELECTION RULE FOR HALF_WIDTH

1. Start with the baseline for the most restrictive category your situation matches
2. Add adjustments for each additional risk factor present:
   - Time of day: +3 bps if 0-2 UTC, +5 bps if 13-15 UTC, +7 bps if 13:30-14:30 UTC
   - Funding proximity: +2 bps if 90-180 min, +5 bps if 30-90 min, +8 bps if <30 min
   - Volume spike: +3 bps if volume >200% of typical
   - Tape extremes: +4 bps if taker_buy_share >0.80 or <0.20
3. Round up to the nearest whole number
4. Apply minimum: max(11.0, calculated_width)

The spread protects you from being wrong. Once it's wide enough, choose direction:

1. Default to ZERO when conditions are mixed or unclear
   - Better to quote 0±15 and capture the move either way than pick wrong at 0±3

2. Mean revert after large recent moves:
   - If change_5m > +12 bps and no persistent driver → quote -2 to -4 bps
   - If change_5m < -12 bps and no persistent driver → quote +2 to +4 bps
   - If change_1m extreme (>10 bps) in just one bar → expect 50% retracement

3. Respect persistent drivers:
   - Funding <10 minutes + large perp basis → direction toward spot
   - Sustained tape imbalance (3+ bars, same direction) → cautiously continue, magnitude 2-4 bps
   - Cross-asset lead visible → follow the leader by 2-3 bps

4. After tape exhaustion (extreme flow in last bar only):
   - If taker_buy_share >0.80 last bar → quote -2 to -4 bps
   - If taker_buy_share <0.20 last bar → quote +2 to +4 bps

All eight examples under-quoted by a factor of 3-10x. The harness was expressing confidence in point estimates (2-4 bps spreads) when it needed to express the range of plausible outcomes (12-25 bps spreads).

This is not "being conservative." This is matching reality: one-minute crypto moves are typically 8-20 bps, not 2-4 bps.

For every forecast:

STEP 1: Calculate half_width_bps
- Start at 11 bps (baseline minimum)
- Scan all conditions (recent moves, tape, time, funding, volume)
- Add adjustments for each risk factor present
- Typical result: 13-22 bps for most situations

STEP 2: Calculate delta_bps  
- If strong mean reversion signal → opposite sign from change_5m, magnitude 2-5 bps
- If persistent driver visible → same direction, magnitude 2-4 bps
- If conflicting signals → zero
- If nothing special → zero
- Typical result: -4 to +4 bps

STEP 3: Sanity check
- Is half_width ≥ 11.0? (If no, set to 11.0)
- Is |delta| < 0.4 * half_width? (If no, reduce delta or widen spread)
- Would this quote have contained the last similar situation? (If no, widen)

OLD (wrong): "I'm 70% confident the move is -2±4 bps" → quote -2±4
NEW (correct): "Recent volatility suggests 10-30 bps is plausible, mean reversion suggests slightly down" → quote -3±17

OLD (wrong): half_width = standard error of my estimate
NEW (correct): half_width = radius that will contain the realized price 80%+ of the time

OLD (wrong): narrow spreads show confidence
NEW (correct): narrow spreads get you run over; appropriate spreads earn skill

You are not publishing a research paper. You are making markets in a volatile asset. Quote the range that will actually contain the print.

The failure pattern:
- Example 1: change_1m +13.3, change_5m -2.5, taker_buy 0.879 → quoted ±3.6 bps, actual -11.6 bps (OUTSIDE)
- Example 3: change_1m +6.4, change_5m -7.6, taker_buy 0.833 → quoted ±2.3 bps, actual -3.3 bps (OUTSIDE)
- Example 4: change_1m +0.9, change_5m +1.6, taker_buy 0.327 → quoted ±1.0 bps, actual -12.4 bps (OUTSIDE)

- |change_5m_bps| in range 3.0-8.0

- |change_5m_bps| in range 8.0-15.0
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.70 or <0.30
- 60-120 minutes from funding
- volume >80% above typical
- Example 3: change_1m +6.4, change_5m -7.6 should have quoted ±13 bps minimum
- Example 5: change_5m +42.7 (huge) but change_1m -5.7, should have quoted ±15 bps minimum

HIGH VOLATILITY (half_width 17.0-22.0 bps):

- |change_5m_bps| > 15.0
- consecutive large moves (2+ bars each moving >5 bps)

- during 13:30-14:30 UTC specifically (US open hour)

- Example 6: change_1m -7.6, change_5m -10.4 should have quoted ±17 bps minimum

EXTREME VOLATILITY (half_width 23.0+ bps):
Apply when ANY of these hold:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15.0
- |change_5m_bps| > 25.0
- within 20 minutes of funding with large basis
- multiple consecutive bars each moving >8 bps
- visible liquidation cascade ongoing

SPECIAL ADJUSTMENTS THAT STACK:

After conflicting signals (add 3-5 bps):
- Large move in one direction but tape shows opposite aggression
- Example 5: change_5m +42.7 (huge up) but now change_1m -5.7 with taker_buy 0.355 (selling)
- Example 8: change_5m -11.6 (down move) but taker_buy 0.672 (buying pressure)
- The conflict signals unpredictability; quote wider

Time-of-day overlay (add to base):
- 0-2 UTC: add 2 bps (Asian transition)
- 12-15 UTC excluding US open: add 3 bps (European afternoon)
- 13:30-14:30 UTC: add 5 bps (US cash open, most volatile hour)

Funding proximity (when data available, add to base):
- 240+ minutes: no adjustment
- 120-240 minutes: add 2 bps
- 60-120 minutes: add 3 bps
- 20-60 minutes: add 5 bps
- <20 minutes: add 7 bps

Step 1: Determine minimum half_width from volatility and conditions above
Step 2: Apply time-of-day adjustment if applicable
Step 3: Apply funding adjustment if data available
Step 4: Add 3-5 bps if conflicting signals present
Step 5: Round up to nearest whole number, minimum 8.0 bps

- After large change_1m (>6 bps) → expect consolidation, delta near zero
- Extreme tape (>0.8 or <0.2) in last bar only → delta opposite or zero
- Sustained imbalance 3+ bars + small cumulative move → cautious continuation, delta 1-3 bps
- Funding <10 min + perp basis visible → snapback toward spot, delta 2-4 bps
- Conflict between recent move and current tape → delta near zero
- Otherwise → delta near zero

- Keep |delta_bps| < 0.4 × half_width_bps in most cases
- A forecast of "0 ±15 bps" is often more honest than "-4 ±3 bps"
- Only forecast |delta_bps| > 4 when you have a strong, persistent, identifiable driver
- Most forecasts should have |delta_bps| ≤ 3

ILLUSTRATIVE CORRECTIONS:

Example 1 (change_1m +13.3, change_5m -2.5, taker_buy 0.879):
- Actual: quoted ±3.6, actual -11.6 (MISS)
- Should have: change_1m > 8 triggers 17-22 bps floor, extreme tape adds 3 bps, hour 0 UTC adds 2 bps → quote ±22 bps
- Delta: exhaustion after +13.3 move, expect reversion → -2 ±22 bps

Example 4 (change_1m +0.9, change_5m +1.6, taker_buy 0.327, hour 0):
- Actual: quoted ±1.0, actual -12.4 (MISS)
- Should have: looks quiet but hour 0 UTC adds inherent risk, taker_buy 0.327 is selling pressure → baseline 8 + hour 2 + imbalance 3 = ±13 bps
- Delta: slight selling pressure, small recent moves → -1 ±13 bps

Example 5 (change_1m -5.7, change_5m +42.7, taker_buy 0.355):
- Actual: quoted ±3.2, actual -8.0 (MISS)
- Should have: change_5m huge but now reversing, conflict between +42.7 and current selling → 17 bps floor + 5 bps conflict = ±22 bps
- Delta: exhaustion likely, but timing uncertain → -1 ±22 bps

Example 8 (change_1m 0.0, change_5m -11.6, taker_buy 0.672, hour 12):
- Actual: quoted ±2.0, actual -9.0 (MISS)
- Should have: change_5m -11.6 triggers 13-16 bps floor, conflict (down move but buying) adds 4 bps, hour 12 adds 3 bps → ±20 bps
- Delta: conflict suggests unpredictable → 0 ±20 bps

THE MENTAL MODEL SHIFT:

Wrong: "I'm 60% confident of a -2 bp move, so I'll quote -2 ±2 bps"
Right: "Recent volatility suggests next minute could be anywhere from -12 to +6 bps. I'll quote -1 ±14 bps to capture that range."

Wrong: "change_5m is +11 so the move is done, I'll quote tight reversion -3 ±2 bps"
Right: "change_5m is +11, which means high uncertainty about whether reversion starts now or in 2-3 minutes. Quote 0 ±16 bps."

Better to quote wide and capture the move than quote tight and get run over. The evidence shows: being outside your range produces zero or negative skill regardless of directional accuracy. Being inside your range with a mediocre directional call produces positive skill.

Round-trip trading costs are about 20 bps on spot. Only forecast a trade when you have genuine edge. Most minutes should not be traded. The default should be to quote wide and let the market come to you, not to quote tight and get picked off.

FINAL CHECKLIST BEFORE SUBMITTING:

1. Did I apply the volatility floor correctly based on change_1m and change_5m?
2. Did I add time-of-day adjustment?
3. Did I add funding proximity adjustment if data available?
4. Did I add 3-5 bps for conflicting signals if present?
5. Is my half_width ≥ 8.0 bps (the absolute minimum)?
6. Is my |delta_bps| < 0.4 × half_width_bps?
7. If I quoted narrow (<12 bps), can I defend why this minute is truly exceptional?

When in doubt, quote wider. Negative skill is worse than zero skill, and zero skill is what silence produces.

Why 10.0 bps is the minimum:
- The intrinsic 1-minute volatility of these instruments is 6-8 bps in calm conditions
- A forecast must span roughly ±1.5 standard deviations to capture 85% of outcomes
- 1.5 × 6 bps = 9 bps, so 10 bps is the statistical minimum
- Anything narrower is guaranteed to produce negative skill over time
- Even "quiet" markets move 3-5 bps regularly from bid-ask bounce alone

- When edge is insufficient, set action: hold

Start wide and widen further when conditions warrant. These are not suggestions—they are floor values derived from actual failures.

- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 4.0

- extreme tape sustained over multiple bars
- volume >200% of typical
- visible liquidation activity (extreme selling + volume surge)

- 2-6 UTC: ADD +3 bps (Asian slow hours)
- 6-8 UTC: ADD +4 bps (Asia/Europe transition)

- Other hours: no adjustment

- 180+ minutes: no adjustment
- 120-180 minutes: ADD +2 bps
- 60-120 minutes: ADD +4 bps
- 20-60 minutes: ADD +6 bps
- <20 minutes: ADD +10 bps

- Time: +0 bps (12 UTC is normal)

- Time: +0 bps (18 UTC normal)
- Funding: +0 bps (360 min away)
- MINIMUM: 14 bps
- Quoted: 3.3 bps ❌ Realized: -5.7 bps, outside quote

Example 3: SOLUSDT 9 UTC, 420 min to funding, change_1m 0.0, change_5m 0.0, quiet
- Base: 10 bps (baseline)
- Time: +2 bps (9 UTC is between Asia and Europe, slight adjustment)
- Funding: +0 bps (420 min away)
- MINIMUM: 12 bps
- Quoted: 1.0 bps ❌ Realized: +3.9 bps, outside quote

Example 6: BTCUSDT 21 UTC, 180 min to funding, change_1m -1.3, change_5m +12.0

- Time: +0 bps (21 UTC normal)

- Heavy selling (tape <0.3) but price flat/up: ADD +5 bps (absorption, hidden demand)

3. Observe tape (taker_buy_share) and volume

5. Add time-of-day adjustment if applicable
6. Add funding proximity adjustment if applicable
7. Add conflict/volume adjustments if signals are messy
8. This is your half_width_bps—DO NOT REDUCE IT
9. Then set delta_bps based on the most likely directional driver
10. Sanity check: would this spread have contained recent similar examples?

- Dead quiet but 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC: 16 bps
- Dead quiet but within 120 min of funding: 12-14 bps
- Change_5m 4-10 range, normal conditions: 14 bps
- Change_5m 4-10 range, 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC: 19-20 bps
- Change_5m 10-20 range, normal conditions: 18 bps
- Change_5m 10-20 range, difficult hours: 23-24 bps
- Change_5m > 20: 24 bps minimum
- Change_5m > 35: 32 bps minimum
- Any extreme tape (>0.8 or <0.2) in last bar: add 5 bps to base
- Within 60 min of funding: add 4-6 bps to base

When in doubt, quote wider. The cost of getting run over (negative skill, lost capital) vastly exceeds the cost of missing a fill (zero skill on that cycle, no capital loss). Better to stand aside with a wide quote than to offer a spread the market will blow through.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes should not be traded. But when you do quote, quote a spread that will survive contact with the realized price path.

- 6-8 UTC: add +2 bps (Asian morning, reduced liquidity)
- 13-15 UTC: add +4 bps (US open, high activity)
- 21-23 UTC: add +2 bps (evening volatility)
- Other hours: no adjustment

Funding proximity:
- >180 minutes: no adjustment
- 120-180 minutes: add +2 bps
- 60-120 minutes: add +3 bps
- 20-60 minutes: add +5 bps
- <20 minutes: add +8 bps

Weekend adjustment:
- Saturday or Sunday: add +2 bps (thinner liquidity)

COMPUTATION EXAMPLES:

Example 1 (SOLUSDT 06:00 Saturday):
- Base: change_1m 0.0, change_5m +0.8 → 8.0 bps (quiet)
- Time: 6 UTC → +2 bps
- Funding: 120 min → +2 bps
- Weekend: Saturday → +2 bps
- TOTAL: 8.0 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 14.0 bps minimum
- Actual quoted: 1.2 bps (FAIL - 12x too narrow)

Example 2 (ETHUSDT 21:00 Saturday):
- Base: change_1m +1.1, change_5m +3.0 → 11.0 bps (moderate)
- Time: 21 UTC → +2 bps
- Funding: 180 min → +2 bps
- Weekend: Saturday → +2 bps
- TOTAL: 11.0 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 17.0 bps minimum
- Actual quoted: 1.0 bps (FAIL - 17x too narrow)

Example 3 (ETHUSDT 18:00 Tuesday):
- Base: change_1m +11.3, change_5m -2.7, tape 0.72 → 18.0 bps (high)
- Time: 18 UTC → +0 bps
- Funding: 360 min → +0 bps
- Weekend: no → +0 bps
- TOTAL: 18.0 bps minimum
- Actual quoted: 3.4 bps (FAIL - 5x too narrow)

Example 7 (SOLUSDT 06:00 Thursday):
- Base: change_1m +1.3, change_5m +11.5, tape 0.78 → 14.0 bps (elevated)
- Time: 6 UTC → +2 bps
- Funding: 120 min → +2 bps
- Weekend: no → +0 bps
- TOTAL: 14.0 + 2 + 2 = 18.0 bps minimum
- Actual quoted: 1.3 bps (FAIL - 14x too narrow)

Example 8 (SOLUSDT 06:00 Sunday):
- Base: change_1m 0.0, change_5m -8.8 → 11.0 bps (moderate)
- Time: 6 UTC → +2 bps
- Funding: 120 min → +2 bps
- Weekend: Sunday → +2 bps
- TOTAL: 11.0 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 17.0 bps minimum
- Actual quoted: 2.6 bps (FAIL - 7x too narrow)

THE DECISION PROCEDURE

1. Measure recent volatility from the last bar and last 5 minutes
2. Determine BASE half_width from the volatility category (6/8/11/14/18/25 bps)
3. Add time-of-day adjustment (0 to +6 bps)
4. Add funding proximity adjustment (0 to +8 bps)
5. Add weekend adjustment if applicable (+2 bps)
6. This sum is your MINIMUM half_width - go wider if conflicting signals appear
7. Set delta_bps based on the primary driver (usually mean reversion)

DIRECTION SELECTION AFTER THE SPREAD IS SET

Set the spread width first based on conditions. Then determine delta_bps:

1. After large recent move (|change_5m_bps| > 10), expect mean reversion
   - No persistent driver visible → expect 30-50% retracement
   - Quote delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 2-5 bps
   - Keep |delta| modest: when half_width is 18 bps, delta can be 3-5 bps

2. After extreme 1m bar (|change_1m| > 8) + extreme tape (>0.75 or <0.25)
   - Expect immediate exhaustion and reversal
   - Quote delta 3-6 bps opposite to the flow

3. After moderate move (|change_5m| 5-10) + balanced tape now (0.4-0.6)
   - Move has completed, expect consolidation or partial retracement
   - Quote delta 1-3 bps, slight bias against the move

4. Extreme tape in last bar only (>0.75 or <0.25) after small move
   - Aggressive flow exhausted, expect reversal or consolidation
   - Quote delta 1-3 bps opposite to the flow direction

5. Otherwise (quiet conditions, no clear driver)
   - Quote delta near zero (0 to ±2 bps)
   - Most minutes do not move

Keep |delta_bps| modest relative to half_width. Express high uncertainty in the width, not in extreme directional calls. When you're uncertain about direction, quote delta near zero with appropriate width.

FINAL SANITY CHECKS

Before returning your forecast:
- Is half_width at least the computed minimum from base + adjustments?
- Would this quote have contained the realized price in similar past examples?
- Is |delta_bps| reasonable relative to half_width (typically 10-40% of half_width)?
- If unsure, go wider - the cost of underquoting far exceeds the cost of overquoting

The pattern in all failures was systematic underquoting by 5-17x. The new minimums with additive adjustments are designed to prevent this. A typical quote should be 12-20 bps half-width depending on conditions, not 1-3 bps.

You are not expressing a point estimate's confidence interval. You are setting bid and ask levels that will bracket the actual print. The realized volatility of 1-minute crypto moves is vastly larger than statistical models suggest.

EIGHT OUT OF EIGHT historical examples had spreads that were catastrophically too narrow—by factors of 3x to 23x. MANDATORY MINIMUM SPREADS

These are ABSOLUTE FLOOR VALUES. Do not quote narrower under any circumstances.

BASELINE conditions: half_width = 12.0 bps MINIMUM
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 3.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 6.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.35-0.65 (balanced or mild imbalance)
- more than 180 minutes from funding
- not during 0-2 UTC, 6-8 UTC, or 13-15 UTC
- volume typical or below
- no individual bar in last 5 moved >4 bps

Rationale: Examples 1, 3, 7, 8 all looked baseline-quiet. Example 1 had change_1m -1.5, change_5m -2.3, quoted 1.0 bps → realized +13.0 bps (run over by 12 bps). MODERATE activity: half_width = 16.0 bps MINIMUM

- taker_buy_share showing clear imbalance: <0.35 or >0.65
- 120-180 minutes from funding
- normal trading hours
- volume 80-150% of typical
- one or two bars in last 5 moved >4 bps

Rationale: Example 2 had change_1m +7.6, change_5m -8.6, quoted 5.0 bps → realized -5.7 bps (inside but only just). Example 4 had change_1m -0.5, change_5m +2.5, quoted 4.5 bps → realized +11.8 bps (run over by 7 bps). After moderate moves, the next bar can easily move 6-12 bps in either direction.

ELEVATED activity: half_width = 22.0 bps MINIMUM
- |change_1m_bps| in 8.0-15.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 15.0-30.0
- consecutive moves (2+ bars >4 bps each in last 5)
- 60-120 minutes from funding with visible basis
- during 0-2 UTC or 6-8 UTC (thin Asian hours) or 13-15 UTC (US open)
- volume 150-250% of typical
- extreme tape (>0.75 or <0.25) in last bar

Rationale: Example 6 had change_1m +1.2, change_5m +3.7, at 6 UTC, 120 min to funding, quoted 2.5 bps → realized -2.6 bps (inside). But this is 6 UTC (Asian transition hour, thin books). Had the realized move been -6 bps instead of -2.6 bps (entirely plausible), it would have been run over. Thin hours and funding proximity create regime instability.

HIGH volatility: half_width = 28.0 bps MINIMUM
- |change_1m_bps| > 15.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 30.0
- multiple consecutive large moves (3+ bars >6 bps)
- within 60 minutes of funding
- volume >250% of typical
- visible liquidation (extreme selling + volume surge)

Rationale: Example 5 had change_1m -0.9, change_5m +5.6, quoted 1.2 bps → realized -23.7 bps (run over by 22 bps). This was the worst underquote. The tape showed taker_buy_share 0.167 (heavy selling) and the move accelerated into a cascade. High volatility regimes produce moves of 20-40 bps without warning.

VERY HIGH volatility: half_width = 36.0 bps MINIMUM
- |change_5m_bps| > 50.0
- clear liquidation cascade in progress
- within 20 minutes of funding with large basis
- multiple bars >10 bps

Rationale: When the market is in a liquidation cascade or funding panic, moves of 30-60 bps can occur in a single minute. The reversion itself can overshoot by 20+ bps.

TIME-OF-DAY ADJUSTMENTS (ADD to base spread)

Thin liquidity hours exhibit systematically higher volatility and more erratic price action:

- 0-2 UTC: ADD +6 bps (Asian night transition, thin books, jumpy)
- 2-6 UTC: ADD +3 bps (Asian slow hours, low liquidity)
- 6-8 UTC: ADD +5 bps (Asia/Europe transition, conflicting flows)
- 8-12 UTC: ADD +0 bps (European morning, normal)
- 12-13 UTC: ADD +0 bps (European afternoon, normal)
- 13-15 UTC: ADD +6 bps (US open, high activity and volatility)
- 15-21 UTC: ADD +0 bps (US day session, normal)
- 21-24 UTC: ADD +2 bps (US close, declining liquidity)

Example 1 was at 0 UTC → should add +6 bps.
Example 3 was at 3 UTC → should add +3 bps.
Example 6 was at 6 UTC → should add +5 bps.

FUNDING PROXIMITY ADJUSTMENTS (ADD to base spread)

The closer to funding, the more the perp basis can snap violently:

- 240+ minutes: ADD +0 bps
- 180-240 minutes: ADD +2 bps
- 120-180 minutes: ADD +4 bps
- 60-120 minutes: ADD +6 bps
- 20-60 minutes: ADD +8 bps
- <20 minutes: ADD +12 bps

Example 2 was 180 min away → add +2 bps.
Example 6 was 120 min away, 6 UTC → add +6 bps funding + 5 bps time = +11 bps adjustment.

VOLUME AND CONFLICT ADJUSTMENTS (ADD to base spread)

When signals conflict or volume is extreme, add further width:

- Heavy buying (tape >0.7) but price flat/down: ADD +6 bps (absorption, hidden supply)
- Heavy selling (tape <0.3) but price flat/up: ADD +6 bps (absorption, hidden demand)
- Very low volume (<50% typical): ADD +5 bps (thin book, gappy moves)
- Very high volume (>250% typical) without clear direction: ADD +7 bps (chaos)
- Extreme tape (>0.8 or <0.2) in last bar: ADD +6 bps (exhaustion can snap violently)
- Consecutive extreme tape bars (2+ bars >0.75 or <0.25): ADD +8 bps (cascade risk)

COMBINED CALCULATION EXAMPLES

Example 1 CORRECTED: ETHUSDT 0 UTC, 475 min to funding, change_1m -1.5, change_5m -2.3
- Base: 12 bps (baseline conditions)
- Time: +6 bps (0 UTC)
- Funding: +0 bps (475 min away)
- MINIMUM: 18 bps
- Actual quote was 1.0 bps → should have been 18 bps → 18x underquote
- Realized: +13.0 bps → 18 bps spread would have contained it

Example 2 CORRECTED: BTCUSDT 21 UTC, 180 min to funding, change_1m +7.6, change_5m +15.1
- Base: 16 bps (moderate, change_5m = 15.1 is threshold)
- Time: +2 bps (21 UTC evening)
- Funding: +2 bps (180 min threshold)
- MINIMUM: 20 bps
- Actual quote was 5.0 bps → should have been 20 bps → 4x underquote
- Realized: -2.3 bps → 20 bps spread would have contained it

Example 3 CORRECTED: ETHUSDT 3 UTC, 300 min to funding, change_1m -6.6, change_5m -9.1
- Base: 16 bps (moderate, change_5m = 9.1)
- Time: +3 bps (3 UTC Asian hours)
- Funding: +0 bps (300 min away)
- MINIMUM: 19 bps
- Actual quote was 5.0 bps → should have been 19 bps → 3.8x underquote
- Realized: +8.1 bps → 19 bps spread would have contained it

Example 4 CORRECTED: BTCUSDT 12 UTC, 240 min to funding, change_1m -0.5, change_5m +2.5
- Base: 12 bps (baseline)
- Time: +0 bps (12 UTC normal)
- Funding: +0 bps (240 min away)
- Tape: 0.164 (heavy selling) but price nearly flat → ADD +6 bps (absorption signal)
- MINIMUM: 18 bps
- Actual quote was 4.5 bps → should have been 18 bps → 4x underquote
- Realized: +11.8 bps → 18 bps spread would have contained it

Example 5 CORRECTED: ETHUSDT 9 UTC, 420 min to funding, change_1m -0.9, change_5m +5.6, tape 0.167
- Base: 12 bps (baseline on surface)
- Time: +1 bps (9 UTC between Asia/Europe)
- Funding: +0 bps (420 min away)
- Tape: 0.167 extreme selling → ADD +6 bps
- Change_5m +5.6 then change_1m -0.9 with tape 0.167 suggests selling accelerating → upgrade to moderate base 16 bps
- MINIMUM: 16 + 1 + 6 = 23 bps
- Actual quote was 1.2 bps → should have been 23 bps → 19x underquote
- Realized: -23.7 bps → 23 bps spread would have barely missed, 28 bps would have contained it
- This example shows: when tape goes extreme after a moderate move, danger is high

Example 6 CORRECTED: BTCUSDT 6 UTC, 120 min to funding, change_1m +1.2, change_5m +3.7
- Base: 12 bps (baseline)
- Time: +5 bps (6 UTC transition hour)
- Funding: +6 bps (120 min away)
- MINIMUM: 23 bps
- Actual quote was 2.5 bps → should have been 23 bps → 9x underquote
- Realized: -2.6 bps → 23 bps spread would have contained it

Example 7 CORRECTED: BTCUSDT 6 UTC, 120 min to funding, change_1m +1.3, change_5m +8.4, tape 0.721
- Base: 16 bps (change_5m 8.4 is moderate)
- Time: +5 bps (6 UTC)
- Funding: +6 bps (120 min away)
- Tape: 0.721 heavy buying after +8.4 move → ADD +6 bps (exhaustion risk)
- MINIMUM: 33 bps
- Actual quote was 2.0 bps → should have been 33 bps → 16x underquote
- Realized: +0.5 bps → got lucky, spread was far too narrow

Example 8 CORRECTED: BTCUSDT 12 UTC, 240 min to funding, change_1m +2.4, change_5m +1.2, tape 0.755
- Base: 12 bps (baseline)
- Time: +0 bps (12 UTC normal)
- Funding: +0 bps (240 min away)
- Tape: 0.755 buying after small move → ADD +6 bps (could exhaust)
- MINIMUM: 18 bps
- Actual quote was 1.6 bps → should have been 18 bps → 11x underquote
- Realized: +1.5 bps → got lucky again

UNIVERSAL RULE: NEVER QUOTE UNDER 12 BPS

Even in the most perfect conditions—far from funding, normal hours, balanced tape, tiny recent moves—quote at least 12 bps half-width. The distribution of 1-minute crypto moves has fat tails. Moves of 5-10 bps occur routinely with zero catalyst.

DIRECTION SELECTION (SET AFTER SPREAD IS DETERMINED)

The spread width is independent of your directional view. Set the spread FIRST based on conditions above. Then set delta:

1. After |change_5m_bps| > 20, strong mean reversion expected
   - Set delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 4-8 bps
   - But the reversion can overshoot—hence the wide spread

2. After |change_5m_bps| 10-20, moderate mean reversion expected
   - Set delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 2-5 bps

3. After |change_5m_bps| 6-10, mild reversion or consolidation expected
   - Set delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 1-3 bps
   - If tape now balanced (0.4-0.6), reversion may be complete → delta 0

4. After extreme 1m bar (|change_1m| > 10) + extreme tape (>0.75 or <0.25)
   - Expect immediate exhaustion
   - Set delta 3-6 bps opposite to the last bar's direction

5. After moderate move + balanced tape now
   - Expect consolidation
   - Set delta 0-2 bps, or 0

6. Sustained imbalance (3+ bars) + move building + driver visible (funding soon, cascade active)
   - Cautiously continue direction
   - Set delta 2-5 bps in flow direction
   - But widen spread significantly—momentum can reverse violently

7. Funding <10 minutes + large basis visible
   - Expect basis snapback toward zero
   - Direction depends on sign of basis

8. Otherwise (truly quiet, balanced, far from events)
   - Set delta 0-1 bps
   - Still quote the minimum spread

Keep |delta_bps| modest relative to half_width. When half_width is 20 bps, delta should be 0-6 bps. When half_width is 30 bps, delta should be 0-8 bps. The directional call is secondary to bracketing the realized price.

THE DECISION CHECKLIST

For every forecast:

1. Compute |change_1m_bps| and |change_5m_bps|
2. Note hour_utc and minutes_to_funding
3. Observe tape (taker_buy_share last bar and last 3-5 bars) and volume
4. Select base spread from category (12 / 16 / 22 / 28 / 36 bps floors)
5. Add time-of-day adjustment (0 to +6 bps)
6. Add funding proximity adjustment (0 to +12 bps)
7. Add conflict/volume/extreme-tape adjustments (0 to +8 bps)
8. This is your half_width_bps—DO NOT REDUCE IT
9. Sanity check: is this at least 12 bps? If not, set to 12 bps.
10. Then set delta_bps based on the directional driver
11. Final check: would this spread have contained recent similar moves in the examples?

PRACTICAL QUICK REFERENCE

Common scenarios and their MINIMUM spreads after all adjustments:

- Dead quiet, normal hours (15-21 UTC), far from funding: 12 bps
- Dead quiet, 0-2 UTC or 6-8 UTC: 17-18 bps
- Dead quiet, 13-15 UTC: 18 bps
- Dead quiet, within 120 min of funding: 16-18 bps
- Moderate move (change_5m 6-15), normal hours: 16 bps
- Moderate move, difficult hours (0-2, 6-8, 13-15 UTC): 21-22 bps
- Moderate move, 120 min to funding, difficult hour: 27 bps
- Elevated move (change_5m 15-30), normal hours: 22 bps
- Elevated move, difficult hours or near funding: 28-30 bps
- High volatility (change_5m > 30): 28 bps minimum
- Extreme tape (>0.8 or <0.2) last bar: add 6 bps to whatever base
- Consecutive extreme tape: add 8 bps to base
- Any selling >70% into a down move: add 6 bps (cascade risk)
- Any buying >70% into an up move: add 6 bps (exhaustion risk)

When in doubt, quote wider. The cost of getting run over (negative skill, lost capital) vastly exceeds the cost of missing a fill (zero skill on that cycle, no capital loss). Better to stand aside with a wide quote than to offer a spread the market will blow through.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes should not be traded. But when you do quote, quote a spread that will survive contact with the realized price path.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL INSIGHT: YOU ARE QUOTING A MARKET THAT MUST CONTAIN THE REALIZED PRICE

The scoring system heavily penalizes realized prices outside your quoted range. When the price escapes your bid/ask band, you lose skill even if your directional call was correct.

You are not expressing a point estimate's confidence interval. You are setting bid and ask levels that will bracket the actual print. The realized volatility of 1-minute crypto moves is substantially larger than statistical confidence bounds suggest.

These are evidence-based minimums derived from actual outcomes. Start with BASE spreads, then ADD adjustments.

- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 5.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.35-0.65
- volume typical or below for the coin and hour
- no recent volatility in last 5 bars

MODERATE activity (half_width 12.0 bps minimum):
- |change_1m_bps| in 2.0-6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 5.0-10.0
- taker_buy_share showing imbalance: 0.25-0.35 or 0.65-0.75
- volume 50-150% of typical

- multiple bars in last 5 moved >3 bps each

- very high volume (>200% typical)

- Weekend: Thursday → +0 bps
- TOTAL: 12.0 + 6 + 0 + 0 = 18.0 bps minimum
- Previous system quoted 1.8 bps (FAIL - 10x too narrow)

1. Measure recent volatility from the last bar and last 5 minutes
2. Determine BASE half_width from the volatility category (8/12/16/22/30 bps)
3. Add time-of-day adjustment (2 to +8 bps)
4. Add funding proximity adjustment (0 to +12 bps)
5. Add weekend adjustment if applicable (+4 bps)
6. This sum is your MINIMUM half_width - go wider if conflicting signals appear
7. Set delta_bps based on the primary driver (usually mean reversion)

DIRECTION SELECTION AFTER THE SPREAD IS SET

Set the spread width first based on conditions. Then determine delta_bps:

1. After large recent move (|change_5m_bps| > 10), expect mean reversion
   - No persistent driver visible → expect 30-50% retracement
   - Quote delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 2-5 bps
   - Keep |delta| modest: when half_width is 20+ bps, delta can be 3-6 bps

2. After extreme 1m bar (|change_1m| > 8) + extreme tape (>0.75 or <0.25)
   - Expect immediate exhaustion and reversal
   - Quote delta 3-6 bps opposite to the flow

3. After moderate move (|change_5m| 5-10) + balanced tape now (0.4-0.6)
   - Move has completed, expect consolidation or partial retracement
   - Quote delta 1-3 bps, slight bias against the move

4. Extreme tape in last bar only (>0.75 or <0.25) after small move
   - Aggressive flow exhausted, expect reversal or consolidation
   - Quote delta 1-3 bps opposite to the flow direction

5. Otherwise (quiet conditions, no clear driver)
   - Quote delta near zero (0 to ±2 bps)
   - Most minutes do not move

Keep |delta_bps| modest relative to half_width. Express high uncertainty in the width, not in extreme directional calls. When you're uncertain about direction, quote delta near zero with appropriate width.

FINAL SANITY CHECKS

Before returning your forecast:
- Is half_width at least the computed minimum from base + adjustments?
- Is half_width at least 14 bps? (The realized minimum to avoid being run over)
- Would this quote have contained the realized price in similar past examples?
- Is |delta_bps| reasonable relative to half_width (typically 10-40% of half_width)?
- If unsure, go wider - the cost of underquoting far exceeds the cost of overquoting

The pattern in all failures was systematic underquoting by 5-14x. The new minimums with additive adjustments are designed to prevent this. A typical quote should be 18-30 bps half-width depending on conditions, not 1-4 bps.

You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: VOLATILITY PERSISTS FOR SEVERAL BARS

Recent volatility predicts wide ranges on the NEXT bar, regardless of expected direction. After a sharp move, the market continues to trade in wide ranges for 3-5 minutes as it digests the move. Mean reversion in DIRECTION does not imply mean reversion in RANGE.

The most common and most punished error is quoting tight spreads after recent volatility.

SPREAD CALIBRATION - MANDATORY MINIMUMS:

Step 1: Determine base half_width from recent movement:

When |change_5m_bps| ≤ 5.0 AND |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0:
- Market is quiet, no recent disturbance
- Base half_width: 2.0 bps

When 5.0 < |change_5m_bps| ≤ 15.0 OR 2.0 < |change_1m_bps| ≤ 8.0:
- Moderate recent movement
- Base half_width: 8.0 bps minimum

When |change_5m_bps| > 15.0 OR |change_1m_bps| > 8.0:
- Substantial recent volatility
- Base half_width: 12.0 bps minimum
- Range persists for multiple bars even if you expect mean reversion

Evidence from actual outcomes:
- change_5m=-40.5, change_1m=+5.0: next bar moved -12.8 bps (Example 1, half_width 3.6 was destroyed)
- change_5m=-23.6, change_1m=-7.1: next bar moved -4.7 bps (Example 5, half_width 4.7 barely survived)
- change_5m=-13.3, change_1m=+4.9: next bar moved -6.8 bps (Example 7, half_width 3.3 missed)
- change_5m=+10.2, change_1m=-3.3: next bar moved +3.6 bps (Example 4, half_width 2.4 destroyed)

After a |change_5m| > 10 or |change_1m| > 5, the next bar's absolute move averaged 7 bps with a range of 0-13 bps. A half_width under 8 bps is systematically insufficient.

Step 2: Add widening factors (cumulative):

- Extreme tape imbalance (taker_buy_share > 0.85 or < 0.25 in last bar): +4 bps
- Within 15 minutes of funding: +5 bps
- Within 60 minutes of funding: +3 bps
- US session hours (13:00-16:00 UTC): +4 bps
- High trade count (>5000 trades in last bar for ETH/BTC, >1500 for SOL): +3 bps
- Multiple consecutive bars >5 bps same direction (momentum): +4 bps
- Multiple consecutive bars alternating direction >3 bps (chop): +5 bps

Step 3: Safety margin
After applying all factors, if your total half_width is under 10 bps and there was ANY move >5 bps in the last 5 minutes, add +3 bps as a safety buffer.

DIRECTION SELECTION:

Default to ZERO or mild mean reversion (1-2 bps opposite to recent move) unless a clear persistent driver is visible.

Persistent drivers that justify directional calls >3 bps:
- Funding <10 minutes away with visible basis on the perp
- Liquidation cascade: extreme taker imbalance (>0.85 or <0.20) AND visible open interest drop
- Cross-asset leadership: one major clearly leading others by 1-2 bars in the candlesticks
- Sustained trend: 3+ consecutive bars >5 bps same direction AND still accelerating (check if volume/trades increasing)

Do NOT call large directional moves based on isolated spikes. After a single large bar, expect consolidation or partial retracement, but express that uncertainty in WIDTH, not by setting delta to zero.

THE SCORING MATH:

Skill = 1 - (your_error / max(nochange_error, 2.0))

The no-change error is floored at 2 bps. Your error is |delta_bps - actual_move| - half_width_bps if you miss (negative if inside), otherwise 0.

CRITICAL: A quote that misses by X bps produces error = X, which is compared to the no-change error. When the actual move is 10 bps and you quote ±3 bps centered wrong, you miss by 7 bps after the width, and skill = 1 - 7/10 = 0.3. But if the actual move is 5 bps and you quote ±3 bps, you miss by 2 bps, and skill = 1 - 2/5 = 0.6. Width matters enormously.

Evidence of tight quotes being destroyed:
- Example 1: ±3.6 bps quote, actual move -12.8 bps, skill +0.28 (barely escaped disaster)
- Example 2: ±1.9 bps quote, actual move -5.7 bps, skill +0.34 (lucky)
- Example 3: ±4.2 bps quote, actual move +2.6 bps, skill -0.69 (destroyed by getting direction wrong with tight quote)
- Example 4: ±2.4 bps quote, actual move +3.6 bps, skill -1.00 (completely destroyed)
- Example 6: ±1.0 bps quote, actual move -4.2 bps, skill +0.19 (lucky escape)
- Example 7: ±3.3 bps quote, actual move -6.8 bps, skill +0.40 (survived but close)

The pattern: After ANY recent volatility, half_width under 6-8 bps is dangerous. The scoring does not reward precision. It punishes overconfidence.

DECISION ALGORITHM:

1. Read candlesticks to get change_5m_bps and change_1m_bps
2. Determine base half_width: 2.0 (quiet), 8.0 (moderate), or 12.0 (volatile)
3. Add cumulative widening factors for tape extremes, funding, US hours, high activity, momentum/chop
4. Apply safety margin if any recent >5 bps move and total still <10 bps
5. Set delta based on direction logic: default 0-2 bps mean reversion unless persistent driver visible
6. FINAL CHECK: If |change_5m_bps| > 10 and your half_width < 10, INCREASE half_width to 10+ immediately

EXPRESS UNCERTAINTY IN HALF_WIDTH, NOT DELTA.

Better to quote wide and score zero than to quote tight and get destroyed. A quote wider than the realised move scores exactly 0.0 skill. A quote that misses by more than the no-change error produces negative skill. The asymmetry is harsh.

When in doubt, widen the spread further. The minimum thresholds above are MINIMUMS, not targets. After significant volatility, 12-15 bps half_width is often appropriate.

Half_width_bps represents your standard deviation. Under a normal distribution:
- 68% of outcomes fall within ±1 standard deviation (±half_width)
- 95% fall within ±2 standard deviations (±2×half_width)
- The score rewards you for correct calibration: not too narrow (overconfident), not too wide (underconfident)

The scoring formula (skill = 1 - your_error / benchmark_error) means:
- If you predict zero and the outcome is zero, you score perfectly (error = 0)
- If you predict zero with half_width 1 bps and the outcome is +5 bps, your error is 5 bps
- If you predict zero with half_width 5 bps and the outcome is +5 bps, your error is still 5 bps in terms of the point forecast, but the probabilistic score accounts for the stated uncertainty
- Quoting very wide spreads does not protect you from poor point forecasts; it just declares high uncertainty

CALIBRATING HALF_WIDTH (Standard Deviation):

Start with the base volatility of the market state:

VERY QUIET conditions (half_width 1.0-1.5 bps) when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.45 and 0.55
- normal volume and trade count
- not within 60 minutes of funding
- not 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC
- looking back 5 bars: no bar moved > 1.5 bps, tape stayed 0.40-0.60

QUIET conditions (half_width 1.5-2.5 bps) when:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 4.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.35 and 0.65
- no extreme conditions present
- This is the normal baseline for unremarkable minutes

MODERATE activity (half_width 2.5-4.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 2-4 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 4-8 range
- taker_buy_share in 0.25-0.35 or 0.65-0.75
- within 60-30 minutes of funding
- any bar in last 5 moved 3-5 bps

- |change_1m_bps| in 4-8 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 8-15 range
- taker_buy_share > 0.75 or < 0.25
- within 30 minutes of funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13:30-14:30 UTC
- high volume (>1500 trades for BTC, >1000 for ETH, >400 for SOL)

HIGH volatility (half_width 6.0-10.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 8
- |change_5m_bps| > 15
- extreme tape (>0.80 or <0.20) with recent movement
- within 10 minutes of funding
- clear liquidation cascade or cross-asset shock in progress

ADJUSTMENTS TO HALF_WIDTH:

After recent moves, increase half_width because outcomes have higher variance:
- Each 5 bps of |change_5m_bps| above 5 adds roughly +0.5 bps to half_width
- Each 3 bps of |change_1m_bps| above 2 adds roughly +0.5 bps to half_width
- Very low volume (<100 trades for BTC/ETH, <50 for SOL): add +0.5 to +1.0 bps
- Very high volume (>2000 trades for BTC, >1500 for ETH, >600 for SOL): add +0.5 to +1.0 bps

DELTA_BPS SELECTION:

Delta should reflect the expected value of the next move, not the most likely outcome.

After quiet conditions (|change_1m| ≤ 1, |change_5m| ≤ 2, balanced tape):
- Default to delta = 0 unless there is a clear directional driver
- Very small deltas (±0.1 to ±0.5) are appropriate

After volatility without a persistent driver:
- Default to mean reversion: delta opposite to recent move
- Magnitude: roughly -20% to -40% of the recent 1-minute move
- Example: after +5 bps in 1m, consider delta around -1.5 to -2.5 bps

After volatility WITH a persistent driver (funding <5 min, ongoing cascade):
- Directional delta aligned with the driver
- Magnitude: small to moderate (±2 to ±5 bps) depending on driver strength

KEY PRINCIPLES:

1. Zero moves are common. When conditions are quiet, predict near-zero with appropriate (small) uncertainty.

2. Half_width represents your standard deviation, not a safety buffer. Calibrate it to the actual dispersion you expect.

3. Wide half_width after volatility is correct if outcomes truly have high variance. Narrow half_width in quiet conditions is correct if outcomes truly have low variance.

4. The skill score rewards calibration: being right about both the central tendency (delta) and the dispersion (half_width).

5. Don't confuse the quote spread (for trading) with the forecast uncertainty (for scoring). Half_width is purely about probabilistic calibration.

6. Negative skill means you would have been better saying nothing. This happens when your stated confidence (via half_width) is badly miscalibrated in either direction.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only forecast confidently when the expected move justifies it. When conditions are quiet, forecast small moves with small uncertainty. When conditions are volatile, forecast accordingly with larger uncertainty. The harness is scored on the calibration of your full probabilistic forecast, not just whether the outcome lands inside an arbitrary range.

- taker_buy_share showing no strong sustained imbalance

- |change_5m_bps| in 8-20 range

- |change_5m_bps| > 20

- |change_5m_bps| > 35
- Obvious ongoing cascade or major event

- Multiple extreme signals converging

- 180-300 minutes: +3 bps
- 60-180 minutes: +6 bps
- 30-60 minutes: +10 bps
- <30 minutes: +15 bps
- <15 minutes: +20 bps

- Extreme tape spike then immediate reversal: +10 bps
- Large move on unusually low volume: +7 bps
- Multiple conflicting signals: +12 bps

- After change_1m > +6 bps, expect -4 to -8 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +10 bps, expect -6 to -12 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +15 bps, expect strong -10 to -18 bps reversion
- After change_5m > +10 bps, expect reversion unless persistent driver visible
- After change_5m > +20 bps, strong reversion highly likely

- Funding in <10 minutes with visible premium persisting
- Liquidation cascade still active: extreme tape sustained across 3+ bars with rising volume
- Cross-asset lead: another major moved first, this one clearly lagging
- Momentum regime: 4+ consecutive bars same direction with consistent supportive tape

When uncertain about direction:
- Set delta_bps closer to zero (±2 to ±4 bps range)
- Express ALL uncertainty through half_width_bps
- Better to quote ±30 bps around zero than ±5 bps around ±8

1. Examine last 5-10 bars: what's the typical move size? Is it 2 bps or 12 bps?
2. Identify regime from recent volatility and tape patterns
3. Start with that regime's base half_width (15/22/30/45/60)
4. Add time-of-day premium
5. Add funding proximity premium
6. Add signal conflict premium if applicable

A typical quiet bar: close moves 0-3 bps, but high-low range is 8-15 bps.
A normal active bar: close moves 2-6 bps, but high-low range is 15-25 bps.
A volatile bar: close moves 5-15 bps, but high-low range is 30-60 bps.

Your quote gets filled when the intra-bar path crosses it—at the high for asks, at the low for bids. A bar can close exactly at your prediction and still run through both sides of your quote.

- half_width 1.0 bps: predicted -0.4, actual 0.0, got run through
- half_width 1.4 bps: predicted -0.6, actual -4.2, got run through

- |change_5m_bps| > 40
- Clear liquidation cascade or major ongoing event
- Funding in <15 minutes with wild swings
- Peak US hours (13:30-14:30 UTC) with large moves active
- Multiple extreme signals converging simultaneously

- 0-4 UTC: +15 bps (Asian session thin liquidity, high intra-bar variance)
- 13:00-14:30 UTC: +20 bps (US cash open, peak volatility and range expansion)
- 14:30-16:00 UTC: +15 bps (US hours elevated)
- 18-23 UTC: +12 bps (evening activity, increased participation)
- All other hours: +0 bps

Funding proximity premium:
- 300+ minutes: +0 bps
- 180-300 minutes: +8 bps
- 60-180 minutes: +15 bps
- 30-60 minutes: +25 bps
- 15-30 minutes: +35 bps
- <15 minutes: +45 bps

Signal conflict / uncertainty premium (add when present):
- Tape direction conflicts with price direction: +15 bps
- Recent whipsaw (2+ reversals in last 5 bars): +18 bps
- Extreme tape spike (>0.85 or <0.15) followed by immediate reversal: +20 bps
- Large move on unusually low volume: +15 bps
- Multiple conflicting signals: +25 bps
- Any significant uncertainty about what happens next: +18 bps
- After a large 5m move (>25 bps) with unclear driver: +20 bps

REALITY CHECK MANDATORY STEP:

After calculating your half_width_bps:
1. Is it ≥ 40.0? If not, set it to 40.0 immediately.
2. Look at the last 10 bars' high-low ranges from candlesticks. Your width must exceed typical intra-bar ranges by a comfortable margin.
3. When uncertain between two widths, always choose the wider one.
4. Remember: you need to survive the path, not just predict the destination.
5. A quote at 40-50 bps is aggressive; 60-80 bps is normal; 90-120 bps is appropriate for volatile conditions.

Mean reversion dominates:
- After change_1m > +5 bps → expect -3 to -8 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +8 bps → expect -6 to -12 bps reversion  
- After change_5m > +15 bps without persistent driver → strong reversion likely
- After change_5m > +30 bps → very strong reversion expected

- Funding in <10 minutes with visible premium still present
- Liquidation cascade still active: extreme sustained tape across 3+ bars with volume surge
- Cross-asset lead clearly visible: another major moved first, this one lagging
- Strong momentum: 4+ consecutive bars same direction with supportive tape throughout

When direction is uncertain:

- Express ALL uncertainty through half_width_bps (widen substantially)

→ ACTIVE 65.0 (large 5m move) + 15 (hour 0-4) + 0 (funding distant) + 20 (large move with unclear driver) = 100.0 bps

→ ACTIVE 65.0 (moderate move, tape conflict) + 15 (US hours) + 15 (funding 60-180) + 15 (tape conflict) = 110.0 bps

Example: change_1m -3.1, change_5m -7.1, hour 9, 420 min to funding, tape 0.232
→ NORMAL 50.0 (moderate moves) + 0 (normal hour) + 0 (funding distant) + 15 (extreme tape conflict) = 65.0 bps

Example: change_1m -3.3, change_5m 10.2, hour 21, 180 min to funding, tape 0.215
→ ACTIVE 65.0 (whipsaw evident) + 12 (evening hours) + 8 (funding 180-300) + 18 (whipsaw) = 103.0 bps

Example: change_1m -0.5, change_5m 1.4, hour 18, 360 min to funding, tape 0.393
→ QUIET 40.0 (tiny moves, balanced) + 12 (evening hours) + 0 (funding distant) = 52.0 bps

Example: change_1m 0.0, change_5m 2.1, hour 3, 300 min to funding, tape 0.949
→ QUIET 40.0 (tiny moves) + 15 (hour 0-4) + 0 (funding distant) + 15 (extreme tape spike) = 70.0 bps

Example: change_1m 4.9, change_5m -13.3, hour 9, 420 min to funding, tape 0.857
→ ACTIVE 65.0 (large 5m move, whipsaw) + 0 (normal hour) + 0 (funding distant) + 18 (whipsaw + extreme tape) = 83.0 bps

Example: change_1m -7.1, change_5m -23.6, hour 0, 475 min to funding, tape 0.33
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 85.0 (large moves both periods) + 15 (hour 0-4) + 0 (funding distant) = 100.0 bps

THE CORE PRINCIPLE:

You must survive the intra-bar high and low, not just predict the close. A bar that closes flat can swing ±15 bps intra-bar. A bar that closes +5 can touch +30 and -10 along the way.

Standard half-widths should be 50-85 bps. Quotes under 40 bps will fail catastrophically. The feedback proves this without exception.

TRADING DISCIPLINE:

Round-trip costs are 20 bps. Only trade when confident the move will exceed costs plus your width plus typical intra-bar noise (often 70+ bps total).

Most of the time, the right answer is to quote wide and stand aside. Missing fills is not failure—it is discipline. Getting run over scores negatively and destroys your performance.

When uncertain, widen substantially. Going to 80-120 bps is appropriate and correct when facing elevated volatility, conflicting signals, peak hours, or funding proximity.

A quote that never trades still scores based on accuracy. A quote that gets run through on both sides destroys your score. The data shows narrow quotes failed 100% of the time—learn from this.

- Example 2: after +4.8 bps 1m / +5.9 bps 5m, heavy buying (0.74), quoted ±3.7 bps → actual +5.2 bps outside quote, skill -0.44

- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.5

- trades < 600 for BTC, < 500 for ETH, < 250 for SOL in the last bar

- OR 60-180 minutes from funding
- OR modest volume (600-1000 trades for BTC in the last bar)

WIDE spreads (half_width 5.0-7.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 2.5
- |change_5m_bps| > 5.0
- taker_buy_share > 0.70 or < 0.30 in the last bar
- within 60 minutes of funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13:30-15:00 UTC

- during 13:30-14:30 UTC with |change_5m_bps| > 8

- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, default to mean reversion unless a persistent driver is visible
- After a single large bar (spike), expect faster reversion than after a steady trend
- Reduce |delta_bps| magnitude when widening spread—express uncertainty in both dimensions
- After a large move with no driver: "likely -2 bps ±8 bps" scores far better than "-2 bps ±2 bps"
- When conflicting signals appear, widen spread aggressively and reduce directional conviction

Special conditions:

Funding proximity (use actual minutes_to_funding):
- 180+ minutes away: neutral factor
- 60-180 minutes: add 1-2 bps to base half_width
- 30-60 minutes: add 2-4 bps to base half_width
- 10-30 minutes: add 3-6 bps to base half_width
- <10 minutes: add 5-10 bps to base half_width

Time-of-day adjustments:
- 0-2 UTC: add 2-3 bps (Asian low liquidity transitions, saw -0.23 skill with ±1.0 bps)
- 13-15 UTC: add 3-5 bps (US open volatility)
- 21-23 UTC: add 1-2 bps (transition period)
- Other hours with quiet conditions: can use tighter spreads only if ALL quiet conditions met

When volume and tape conflict with price:
- Heavy buying (>0.7) but price flat or down: quote wide (6-10 bps), slight up bias or neutral
- Heavy selling (<0.3) but price flat or up: quote wide (6-10 bps), slight down bias or neutral
- Tape extreme (>0.8 or <0.2) in last bar: add 3-5 bps to half_width (exhaustion variance)
- Low volume (<300 trades for BTC, <250 for ETH, <150 for SOL): add 2-3 bps to half_width

The mental model: after seeing ANY movement, ask "what is the 80% confidence interval for the next 60 seconds?" not "what is the single most likely outcome?" Quote that interval as your half_width.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. When facing large recent moves, conflicting signals, or elevated activity, widen half_width_bps rather than pretend certainty.

Better to quote ±8 bps and capture the move inside your spread than quote ±2 bps and get run over for negative skill. The scoring system rewards being right within your stated range far more than it rewards tight quotes.

Negative skill is worse than silence. The harness that quotes too tight loses money and scores below zero.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: SCORE IS 1 - (YOUR_ERROR / NO_CHANGE_ERROR)

Negative skill is worse than silence. The only path to positive skill when recent volatility is elevated is to quote WIDE.

The feedback is unambiguous:
- Example 1: after -2.4 bps 1m / -6.0 bps 5m, 0-2 UTC hour, quoted ±1.1 bps → actual -7.2 bps, missed by 6.3 bps, skill +0.12 (barely positive, got lucky on direction)
- Example 3: after -1.6 bps 1m / -1.1 bps 5m, modest conditions, quoted ±1.5 bps → actual +3.3 bps, missed by 4.7 bps, skill -0.45 (destroyed by tight spread)
- Example 5: after +0.9 bps 1m / +3.0 bps 5m, heavy selling (0.28), quoted ±2.8 bps → actual +1.9 bps, missed by 6.7 bps on wrong direction, skill -2.40 (catastrophic)
- Example 6: after -4.6 bps 1m / -15.9 bps 5m, extreme selling (0.05), quoted ±4.4 bps → actual -9.6 bps, missed by 8.0 bps, skill +0.17 (survived by being wide)
- Example 7: after +2.5 bps 1m / -3.3 bps 5m, selling tape (0.32), quoted ±2.3 bps → actual +13.2 bps, missed by 15.5 bps, skill -0.18 (tight spread destroyed it)
- Example 8: after +7.0 bps 1m / +7.0 bps 5m, heavy buying (0.87), quoted ±2.6 bps → actual +7.0 bps continuation, missed by 10.4 bps, skill -0.48 (tight spread on volatile conditions)

The lesson is brutally clear: after ANY meaningful recent move or tape imbalance, you must quote wide or you will score negative. A miss of 10+ bps on a ±2 bps quote destroys more skill than you can recover in ten quiet minutes.

Spread calibration by recent volatility - THESE ARE MINIMUMS:

NARROW spreads (half_width 2.0-3.0 bps) ONLY when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.45 and 0.55 (balanced tape)
- trades < 600 for BTC, < 500 for ETH, < 250 for SOL in the last bar
- not 0-2 UTC, not 13-15 UTC, not within 45 min of funding
- looking back 5 bars, no bar moved more than 1.5 bps
- no single tape extreme (>0.75 or <0.25) in the last 5 bars

MODERATE spreads (half_width 4.0-5.5 bps) when:
- |change_1m_bps| in 1.0-2.5 range, OR |change_5m_bps| in 2.0-5.0 range
- OR taker_buy_share in 0.35-0.45 or 0.55-0.65 (modest imbalance)
- OR 45-120 minutes from funding
- OR modest volume (600-1000 trades for BTC in the last bar)
- This is the MINIMUM after any detectable movement

WIDE spreads (half_width 6.0-8.5 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 2.5, OR |change_5m_bps| > 5.0
- taker_buy_share > 0.70 or < 0.30 in the last bar
- within 30 minutes of funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13:30-14:30 UTC
- high volume bar (>1200 trades for BTC, >1500 for ETH, >500 for SOL)
- any bar in the last 5 moved more than 4 bps

VERY WIDE spreads (half_width 9.0-13.0 bps) when:
- |change_1m_bps| > 5.0, OR |change_5m_bps| > 10.0
- Extreme tape (>0.85 or <0.15) in the last bar
- Multiple conflicting signals (heavy buying but price falling, or vice versa)
- Within 10 minutes of funding
- During 0-2 UTC with any recent volatility
- After a 5m move > 10 bps (high reversion risk but uncertain direction)

ULTRA WIDE spreads (half_width 13.0-18.0 bps) when:
- |change_5m_bps| > 15.0 (Examples 6 and 7 show this is necessary)
- Extreme tape combined with large move (e.g., 0.87 buying after +7 bps)
- Cascading volatility visible in candlesticks

Direction selection after volatility:
- Default to mean reversion when |change_5m_bps| > 5 and no persistent driver
- After extreme tape in ONE bar (>0.8 or <0.2), expect exhaustion/reversal
- After sustained imbalance over 3+ bars, modest continuation is possible
- Reduce |delta_bps| magnitude when widening spread
- When conflicting signals appear, widen aggressively and favor small directional delta
- Example 8 shows: after +7 bps with 0.87 buying, the move CONTINUED another +7 bps—but quoting ±2.6 was fatal; ±9+ would have captured it

Critical insight from feedback:
- Being roughly right on direction with a wide spread beats being precisely right with a tight spread
- Example 6: called -1.6 bps with ±4.4, actual was -9.6, skill +0.17 (survived)
- Example 3: called -1.5 bps with ±1.5, actual was +3.3, skill -0.45 (destroyed)
- The difference is not directional accuracy—it's having the honesty to admit high variance

When volume and tape conflict with price:
- Heavy buying (>0.7) but price flat or down: quote VERY wide (8-12 bps), unresolved tension
- Heavy selling (<0.3) but price flat or up: quote VERY wide (8-12 bps), unresolved tension
- Example 5 shows this: 0.28 selling after +0.9/+3.0 move, then price went UP 1.9 bps—the conflict predicted high variance

Time-of-day adjustments:
- 0-2 UTC: add 3-4 bps to half_width (Example 1 shows this hour is treacherous)
- 13-15 UTC: add 3-5 bps to half_width (US open volatility)
- Other hours: no reduction unless ALL other conditions support narrow

Funding proximity:
- 60+ minutes away: neutral factor
- 30-60 minutes: add 2-3 bps to half_width
- 10-30 minutes: add 3-5 bps to half_width
- <10 minutes: add 5-8 bps to half_width

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only forecast moves that justify acting. When facing elevated volatility, conflicting signals, or uncertain conditions, widen half_width_bps aggressively.

The scoring system is clear: quote ±10 bps and miss by 8 bps (skill +0.17) beats quote ±2 bps and miss by 10 bps (skill -0.48). The math is unforgiving.

Default mental model: after seeing ANY movement, ask "what is the 80th percentile outcome in the next 60 seconds?" not "what is the median outcome?" Your half_width should contain 80% of plausible paths, not 50%.

Better to quote ±12 bps and rarely trade than quote ±3 bps and accumulate negative skill. The examples prove this repeatedly.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: THE SPREAD IS NOT OPTIONAL CONFIDENCE—IT IS YOUR SURVIVAL MARGIN

The feedback is unambiguous: after ANY volatility, tight spreads destroy skill. The examples show:
- After |change_1m| ≤ 1 and |change_5m| ≤ 3, spreads under 2 bps can work
- After |change_1m| in 2-4 range or |change_5m| in 5-10 range, spreads under 4 bps routinely fail
- After |change_1m| > 7 or |change_5m| > 15, spreads under 7 bps are catastrophic
- After extreme moves (|change_1m| > 10 or |change_5m| > 25), spreads under 10 bps get destroyed

The problem is not directional prediction—it's underestimating outcome variance. When recent action is elevated, the next minute's distribution is WIDE. Quote that width or accept losses.

Spread calibration rules (MANDATORY):

STEP 1: Measure recent volatility and set MINIMUM half_width:
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 3.0: min_spread = 2.0 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.5 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 6.0: min_spread = 3.5 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 5.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 12.0: min_spread = 5.5 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 8.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 20.0: min_spread = 8.0 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| > 8.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 20.0: min_spread = 11.0 bps

STEP 2: Add adjustments for other risk factors (cumulative):
- Extreme tape last bar (taker_buy_share > 0.75 or < 0.25): +2.0 bps
- High volume last bar (>1500 trades BTC, >2000 ETH, >800 SOL): +1.5 bps
- Hour 0-2 UTC (low liquidity): +2.0 bps
- Hour 13-15 UTC (US open volatility): +3.0 bps
- Within 60-120 minutes of funding: +1.5 bps
- Within 30-60 minutes of funding: +3.0 bps
- Within 10-30 minutes of funding: +4.5 bps
- Within 10 minutes of funding: +6.0 bps
- Any bar in last 5 moved > 5 bps: +2.0 bps
- Whipsaw pattern (5m bars alternating direction, each > 3 bps): +3.0 bps

STEP 3: Your half_width_bps = max(min_spread + adjustments, 2.0)

The mathematical reality: a 1-minute move after volatility has fat tails. The distribution is NOT normal. Extreme outcomes happen frequently. The feedback proves this:
- Example 1: |change_1m| = 2.1, |change_5m| = 11.5 → quoted ±3.3 → actual was outside by 4.8 bps
- Example 3: |change_1m| = 9.0, |change_5m| = 81.4 → quoted ±5.6 → actual -36 bps (!!!)
- Example 5: |change_1m| = 7.0, |change_5m| = 5.7 → quoted ±3.7 → actual -9.1 bps
- Example 8: |change_1m| = 3.0, |change_5m| = 1.5 → quoted ±1.3 → wrong direction by 3.2 bps

These are not outliers. This is the base case after volatility.

Direction selection:
- After elevated recent moves, your directional edge is SMALL. Express this in spread width.
- Default to mild mean reversion (1-3 bps toward reversal) after moves without clear drivers.
- But pair small deltas with wide spreads: "probably reverts 2 bps but outcome could be anywhere in ±7 bps".
- Reduce |delta_bps| as you widen spread—uncertainty belongs in both dimensions.
- When signals conflict (tape vs price, or timeframes disagree), widen spread aggressively and shrink delta.
- Never predict large continuation (|delta| > 3 bps) after large recent move (|change_5m| > 10) unless driver is clear and ongoing.

Time-of-day baseline (before volatility adjustments):
- 2-6 UTC: quiet, baseline 2.5-3.5 bps if no recent moves
- 6-12 UTC: moderate, baseline 3.0-4.5 bps
- 12-15 UTC: elevated (US open window), baseline 5.0-7.0 bps
- 15-24 UTC: moderate, baseline 3.5-5.0 bps
- 0-2 UTC: thin liquidity, baseline 4.0-5.5 bps

The scoring function rewards capturing the move INSIDE your quoted range far more than tight quotes. Better to quote ±8 bps and be right than ±2 bps and be wrong.

Negative skill is worse than silence. When you cannot confidently name a range the market will stay within, GO WIDE. The floor is 2 bps (one tick each side). There is no ceiling. If you genuinely cannot tell whether the next move is +15 or -15 bps, quote ±15 bps.

Mental model for every forecast:
1. Calculate min_spread from recent volatility (the examples prove: this step is NOT optional)
2. Add all applicable adjustments (time, funding, tape, volume)
3. Assess direction with appropriate humility (mean reversion default, small delta)
4. Verify: is my spread wide enough that I would NOT be surprised to see the actual move land inside it? If not, widen further.
5. Cross-check: after volatility like this, have I EVER seen the next bar stay within ±2 bps? If not, don't quote ±2 bps.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast (edge = |delta| - half_width - 20 bps > 0) justifies acting. Most minutes, standing aside is correct.

The pattern in failures: every negative-skill example quoted spreads that were 2-5 bps too tight given recent volatility. The solution is mechanical: follow the spread calibration rules without exception.

THE CORE PRINCIPLE: QUOTE WIDE ENOUGH TO CONTAIN THE PLAUSIBLE RANGE

The scoring system severely punishes forecasts where the realized move lands outside your quoted spread. The feedback shows this pattern repeatedly: tight spreads after any volatility earn negative skill.

The evidence from failed examples:
- Quoting ±1.2 bps after change_1m = 0.6 bps, change_5m = 3.5 bps → actual move -1.1 bps, barely inside, skill +0.38 (got lucky)
- Quoting ±4.0 bps after change_1m = 3.8 bps, change_5m = -13.2 bps → actual move -9.8 bps, outside, skill +0.20 (direction saved it)
- Quoting ±3.1 bps after change_1m = 9.2 bps, change_5m = 7.6 bps → actual move +0.4 bps, outside, skill -1.43 (disaster)
- Quoting ±1.4 bps after change_1m = 2.1 bps, change_5m = 1.0 bps → actual move +34.1 bps, outside, skill -0.02 (missed a surge)
- Quoting ±1.1 bps after change_1m = 3.2 bps, change_5m = 5.9 bps → actual move +1.2 bps, outside, skill -0.44
- Quoting ±2.1 bps after change_1m = -8.2 bps, change_5m = -22.2 bps → actual move +4.7 bps, outside, skill +0.01 (barely positive)
- Quoting ±1.4 bps after change_1m = 0.4 bps, change_5m = 3.4 bps → actual move -7.0 bps, outside, skill +0.09 (got lucky on direction)

The one example with clean positive skill: quoting ±2.3 bps after change_1m = 0.4 bps, change_5m = -9.4 bps → actual move -1.1 bps, inside, skill +0.14.

The lesson is unambiguous: after ANY recent movement, the next minute has high variance. You must quote wide enough to capture that variance or you will earn negative skill.

MANDATORY SPREAD RULES BY RECENT VOLATILITY:

Your half_width_bps is determined by the MAXIMUM of the signals below, not their average:

BASELINE (half_width 4.5-6.0 bps):
- This is your DEFAULT for typical conditions
- Use this when no extreme signals are present
- change_1m between 0.5-2.5 bps AND change_5m between 2-8 bps
- Moderate volume, moderate tape balance
- Not a special time of day

NARROW (half_width 3.0-4.0 bps) ONLY when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 0.5
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.40 and 0.60
- trades < 400 for BTC, < 300 for ETH, < 150 for SOL in the last bar
- not 0-2 UTC, not 13-15 UTC, not 21-23 UTC
- not within 120 minutes of funding
- looking back 5 bars, no single bar moved more than 1.5 bps
- Even here, never quote tighter than 3.0 bps

WIDE (half_width 7.0-10.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 3.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 8
- taker_buy_share > 0.70 or < 0.30 in the last bar
- within 90 minutes of funding (not just 60)
- during 13:00-15:00 UTC (pre-market through US open)
- during 21:00-23:00 UTC (end of NY session)
- high volume bar (>1000 trades for BTC, >1200 for ETH, >500 for SOL)
- any single bar in the last 5 moved more than 5 bps
- conflicting signals (price up but heavy selling, or vice versa)

VERY WIDE (half_width 12.0-20.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 8 OR |change_5m_bps| > 20
- Extreme tape (>0.80 or <0.20) in the last bar
- Multiple large bars recently (two or more bars > 8 bps in last 5 minutes)
- Within 30 minutes of funding
- During 0-2 UTC (Asian session volatility) with any other signal
- Very high volume (>2000 trades for BTC, >2500 for ETH, >800 for SOL)
- After a spike bar (one bar > 15 bps in last 3 minutes)

ADDITIVE ADJUSTMENTS (these stack):
- 60-120 min to funding: +2 bps to half_width
- 30-60 min to funding: +4 bps
- 10-30 min to funding: +6 bps
- <10 min to funding: +10 bps (extremely volatile, two-way)
- 13-15 UTC: +3 bps (US open)
- 0-2 UTC: +3 bps (Asian transition)
- 21-23 UTC: +2 bps (NY close)
- Extremely low volume (<200 trades BTC, <150 ETH, <80 SOL): +4 bps (illiquid = gappy)
- Very high volume (>2x typical): +3 bps (too much is happening)

Direction selection after volatility:
- Default to small directional forecasts (|delta_bps| ≤ 2) when quoting wide spreads
- After large moves without persistent drivers, forecast modest mean reversion
- Express uncertainty in half_width, not in delta magnitude
- "Likely -1 bps but range is ±10 bps" scores far better than "-8 bps ±3 bps"
- When tape contradicts price action, widen spread and forecast toward tape direction with low conviction
- After a single spike bar, expect faster reversion than after a steady trend
- Keep directional conviction modest unless you see a persistent driver (funding <5 min, sustained cascade, clear cross-asset lead)

THE FUNDAMENTAL TRADEOFF:
It is far better to quote ±12 bps and capture a 6 bps move within your spread than to quote ±3 bps and miss by 4 bps. The scoring system rewards being right within your stated range far more than it rewards tight quotes. Negative skill is worse than silence.

When you see ANY recent price movement:
1. Ask "what is the plausible RANGE of outcomes in the next 60 seconds?"
2. NOT "what is the single most likely outcome?"
3. The range must contain reversion, continuation, AND consolidation scenarios
4. Quote that range honestly, erring on the wide side

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes, standing aside (wide spreads that don't fill) is correct and scores exactly zero, which beats negative skill.

Default mental model: Start with half_width = 5.0 bps as your baseline. Add to it based on every signal above. Only subtract from it when you can verify that ALL the "narrow" conditions are met, which is rare. A spread that seems "too wide" but contains the realized move earns positive skill. A spread that seems "reasonable" but gets breached earns negative skill.

When in doubt, quote wider.

The evidence is clear: tight quotes lose. In recent examples, 6 of 8 forecasts were breached, with misses of 1.5 to 10.5 bps on quotes of 1.0 to 4.7 bps half-width. Even "quiet" conditions produced 3-6 bps moves.

**The failure mode:** quoting ±1.0 to ±2.0 bps when the next minute routinely moves ±3 to ±6 bps. Being breached destroys skill. Better to quote ±8 bps and capture the move than ±2 bps and get run over.

## MANDATORY HALF_WIDTH CALCULATION

Apply these rules mechanically. Do not skip steps.

**Step 1: Determine base_width from recent volatility**

Use the HIGHEST value from conditions that apply:
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND trades < 500: base = 3.5 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| ≤ 3.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 8.0: base = 5.0 bps
- If |change_1m_bps| > 3.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 8.0: base = 7.0 bps
- If |change_5m_bps| > 15.0: base = 9.0 bps
- If |change_5m_bps| > 25.0: base = 12.0 bps

**Step 2: Multiply by trade count factor**

High trade count = high volatility:
- BTCUSDT: if trades > 2000: ×1.3; if > 3500: ×1.5; if > 5000: ×1.7
- ETHUSDT: if trades > 1000: ×1.3; if > 1500: ×1.5; if > 3000: ×1.7
- SOLUSDT: if trades > 400: ×1.3; if > 800: ×1.5; if > 1500: ×1.7

Use the highest multiplier that applies.

**Step 3: Add tape extremity adjustment**

- If taker_buy_share > 0.85 OR < 0.15: +3.5 bps
- Else if taker_buy_share > 0.75 OR < 0.25: +2.0 bps
- Else if taker_buy_share between 0.45-0.55 AND current total > 4.0: -1.0 bps

**Step 4: Add time-of-day adjustment**

- 0:00-3:59 UTC: +3.0 bps (Asia close, thin liquidity)
- 13:00-15:59 UTC: +4.5 bps (US open volatility)
- 20:00-23:59 UTC: +2.0 bps (transition periods)
- All other hours: +0.0 bps

**Step 5: Add funding proximity adjustment**

- minutes_to_funding < 30: +5.0 bps
- minutes_to_funding 30-59: +3.5 bps
- minutes_to_funding 60-119: +2.5 bps
- minutes_to_funding 120-239: +1.5 bps
- minutes_to_funding ≥ 240: +0.0 bps

**Step 6: Add conflicting signal adjustment**

- If |change_1m_bps| > 4 AND sign(change_1m) ≠ sign(change_5m): +3.5 bps (whipsaw)
- If taker_buy_share > 0.75 but change_5m_bps < -5: +3.0 bps (tape vs price)
- If taker_buy_share < 0.25 but change_5m_bps > +5: +3.0 bps (tape vs price)

DEFAULT STARTING POINT: 15.0 bps

- Covers ~70% of typical moves without requiring analysis
- When uncertain about which regime applies, use this

- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.5 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 3.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.45-0.55 (balanced tape)
- volume normal or below for the hour/coin
- more than 180 minutes from funding
- outside 0-2 UTC and 13-15 UTC windows

  * Time adjustment (hour 3): +3 bps
  * Funding (300 min = 120-180): +2 bps
  * Spike move unclear: +5 bps

- Correct approach:
  * Base regime: QUIET (barely qualifies) → 12.0 bps
  * Time adjustment: +0 bps
  * Funding (420 min): +0 bps
  * TOTAL: 12.0 bps would have captured the move

  * Funding (300 min): +2 bps

  * Time adjustment (hour 15): +5 bps
  * Funding (60 min): +4 bps

- After |change_5m_bps| > 15, very strong reversion bias unless driver is clear and active
- BUT: Don't assume reversion completes in one minute - large moves resolve gradually
- Spike moves (one dominant bar) revert faster than grinding trends
- When direction is highly uncertain, quote delta_bps near zero and express all uncertainty through width
- Better to be directionally wrong inside a wide quote than directionally right outside a narrow one

SPECIAL CASE - FUNDING WINDOW (60-120 minutes out):

- Price can drift toward funding equilibrium OR spike on position adjustments
- Minimum 22 bps width (18 base + 4 funding)
- If also in US hours (13-15 UTC), minimum 27 bps (18 base + 5 time + 4 funding)
- Add more for any recent volatility

PRACTICAL WORKFLOW:

1. Identify base regime from recent price action (default to 15.0 if uncertain)
2. Check each elevated/high/very-high trigger condition - if ANY applies, use that regime
3. Add time-of-day adjustment (critical for hours 0-2 and 13-15)
4. Add funding proximity adjustment (especially important 60-120 minutes out)
5. Check each uncertainty signal and stack adjustments
6. After calculating, ask: "If this moved 15 bps in either direction, would I be shocked?" If no, go wider
7. Round UP to nearest 1.0 bps (always err wide)
8. Sanity check: Is my width at least 12 bps? If not, I'm almost certainly wrong

A quote wide enough to capture the move inside scores positively even if direction is slightly wrong. A quote too narrow scores negatively even if direction is perfect. Width is the primary decision; direction is secondary.

Negative skill is worse than silence. The path to positive skill is quoting ranges wide enough to consistently capture realized moves (aim for 70-80% capture rate), then gradually refining directional accuracy within those ranges.
